cases.description: Label wording equals the JSON key. Every deterministic matcher should pass.
Same facts asked in different words; keys are not worded like the questions.
Sibling values that differ only by a scope word. Related values must not be confused.
Deep paths, repeated sub-objects (hq/billing), lists of objects, section headings.
Yes/No questions worded many ways, plus a negation trap and CAIQ-style Yes/No/NA.
Source value must be mapped onto the form's own option list.
Two or more plausible values. The safe outcome is REVIEW unless the question disambiguates.
Answer not in the source, plus near-miss keys that tempt a false positive.
Free-text questions: direct answer present, composition required, or nothing relevant.
Fields revealed by earlier answers, two-level chains, hidden-must-stay-hidden, and a conditional whose trigger is worded as a paraphrase.
Three-step wizard: step 2 hidden in the DOM, step 3 rendered only after Next.
Source values that violate (or can be coerced into) the control's constraints.
SIG/CAIQ-style page: ID-prefixed labels, domain sections, Yes/No/NA, engineer-style nested source whose booleans are named `exists`/`enabled`.
The same easy facts, but each label is attached to its control a different way.
Controls that are not native inputs (ARIA widgets, contenteditable, open shadow DOM, file upload).
Native inputs that behave dynamically: read-only picker, input mask, late options, enabled-by-answer.
